parsed.stack: Android-first (Flutter/Dart) because UK HGV drivers are overwhelmingly Android, which means Apple's free Private Cloud Compute tier does NOT apply and every minute is paid; cheap streaming ASR + frontier text model for the conversation, on-device TTS for the voice back; note delivery to the household by email/SMS via Postmark; FastAPI + Postgres on Hetzner (EU data residency); Google Play + App Store.
milestones: Week 1-2: hands-free wind-down recorder with a hard 10-minute timer, offline buffering for depot yards and motorway dead spots.
Week 3-4: conversational turn-taking tuned for a moving cab, with barge-in and a wake phrase that survives road noise.
Week 5-6: the morning note - one short written summary generated overnight and delivered to a household address before breakfast, with the driver able to redact before it sends.
Week 7-8: household-side install flow (the gift_to_recipient loop), subscription at GBP 6 via RevenueCat, and per-user minute metering with a visible cost ceiling.
Week 9-10: Play/App Store review, DVSA-safe UI review (nothing requiring a touch while moving), 15-driver depot pilot.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That a ten-minute nightly spoken session can be served for under about $0.30 per active driver - it cannot: 15 nights x 10 minutes is 150 minutes, which is $0.75 at the cheapest $0.005/min stack and $2.70 at $0.018, against $0.23 of blended revenue per active at GBP 6 and 3% conversion, so this idea fails its own fourth kill criterion on arithmetic before any code is written.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: No build needed - price one week of the intended session length against the cheapest usable voice vendor on a spreadsheet, then, if you still want it, test whether drivers accept a 3-minute cap instead of 10 by running 10 drivers through a WhatsApp voice-note version for two weeks at effectively zero cost.
